slides.title: Conversation control
slides.subtitle: Sign in mid-conversation, talk directly, hand off to a person, close
slides.notes: A conversation is more than messages. This example drives one Manzanita conversation through four controls: signing in part-way through, a Direct Conversation, a handoff to a person at the support desk, and closing.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] U["Ada, the user"] subgraph HOST["Atlas's host, trusted"] direction TB A["Atlas
personal agent"] -- "keeps" --> T[("Tokens, device code")] end subgraph CO["Manzanita"] direction TB C["Conversation"] -- "handoff" --> D["Support desk
people"] end U -- "asks" --> HOST U -- "approves device code" --> CO HOST -- "messages and controls" --> CO HOST -. "events, statuses, errors" .-> M
slides.caption: Atlas drives the conversation; the model sees what happened, never the tokens behind it.
slides.notes: Ada is the user. She asks Atlas, her personal agent, and once she approves a device code on Manzanita's own page. Atlas's host keeps the tokens and the device code, and sends Manzanita the messages and the controls: sign-in, a Direct Conversation, a handoff and a close. Inside Manzanita, a handoff reaches people at its support desk, staffed in this example. Off to the side, the model receives event types, statuses and error codes it can explain to Ada, never the tokens.

slides.title: Sign-in mid-conversation

items.title: Ask
items.detail: Where is my jacket order? Signed out

items.title: Same conversation
items.detail: Same Session signed in, same conversation ID

slides.notes: Signed out, Manzanita cannot look up an order, so it answers with an authorization event: insufficient_scope, with the scope the request needs. The host signs Ada in for that scope with a mode the company offers, here device sign-in, and keeps sending to the same conversation ID, in the same Session, with the new access token.

slides.title: A Direct Conversation
slides.notes: Only the personal agent starts a Direct Conversation, so the user can talk with the company in the agent's own interface. While it is open, the parent refuses messages and handoff with direct_conversation_open, and the SDK puts the open conversation's ID in the error details.

slides.title: Handoff, then close

items.title: handoff()
items.detail: Ask for a person at the company

slides.notes: A handoff puts the conversation in the queued state until a person takes it; then the responder is human, and each of their messages names its author: type human, with the person's id and name when the company gives them. When nobody is available, the company says so and the agent carries on. Closing ends the conversation, but it doesn't cancel anything the conversation started, such as an order or a return.

slides.title: The conversation's status
slides.diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> working: message
  working --> idle: answered
  idle --> working: next message
  idle --> queued: handoff
  queued --> idle: a person takes it
  idle --> closed: close
  closed --> [*]
slides.caption: After a handoff the responder is human; closing does not cancel what the conversation started.
slides.notes: Follow the parent conversation's status. A message makes it working, and the answer leaves it idle, ready for the next one. Signing in part-way through keeps the same conversation ID, so the loop just continues with the new token. A handoff puts it in queued until a person at the support desk takes it; then it is idle again, with the responder human. If nobody is available, the company says so and the agent carries on. Close ends it: later messages draw conversation_closed, and nothing the conversation started is cancelled.

slides.title: What stays where

left.heading: Host-only
items: The user code, shown by the host

slides.notes: The model sees what happened, never the means. Tokens, the device code and Session JWTs stay in the host, and the user code is shown to the user by the host, not by the model.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI and Agent Runtimes examples drive one Manzanita conversation through all four
slides.notes: Run the Pydantic AI example with PAP_EXAMPLE_MODEL set to the model you want. TypeScript has startDirect, handoff and close on ConversationClient, with the same error codes and details.
